findings.title: Care that returns inward
findings.claim: The parental-care commands in 17:23-24 turn 17:25 from outward conduct toward inner state, righteousness, repeated return, and forgiveness. Read together, the remembered care of childhood can return as care for aging parents, while forgiveness remains open to those who turn back.
findings.mechanism: Verse 17:23 regulates what is said and done as parents reach old age; 17:24 recalls that they raised the addressee when small and asks for mercy; 17:25 names the selves within, a righteous condition, returners, and divine forgiveness. The care relationship reverses direction, and the focus attaches forgiveness to the returning person.
findings.reader_payoff: Return becomes legible within a relationship of received and returned care, with divine forgiveness keeping repair possible after strained conduct.
findings.containment: The plain statement remains that God knows what is within and forgives returners. The context describes duties and a prayer; it does not establish that any addressee failed in parental care or define al-awwabin as caregivers.

epistemic.reason: The channel packet supplies exact focus branches and the adjacent parental-care scene; the integrated care-return relation is a contextual synthesis, not an adjudicated recurring system.
